newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FIGURE SKATING-CHAMPION ELDREDGE MAKES STRONG START.
newsitem.headline: FIGURE SKATING-CHAMPION ELDREDGE MAKES STRONG START.

text.p: Title holder Todd Eldredge drew first blood against Elvis Stojko, the man he deposed last year, when the world figure skating championships began on Sunday.

American Eldredge and Canadian Stojko both fell during their routines but Eldredge emerged with a victory in the first group of qualifying which will reduce the field from 45 to 30 for the men's main event which begins on Wednesday.
Viacheslav Zagorodniuk of Ukraine took third place with Andrei Vlascenko of Germany fourth ahead of Azerbaijani Igor Pashkevitch and Russian Alexei Yagudin, 17 earlier this month.
The second qualifying group, which contains Olympic and European champion Alexei Urmanov and fellow Russian Ilya Kulik, was set for later on Sunday.
Eldredge, nursing a sprained ankle he suffered landing a triple axel jump in practice 10 days ago, fell on that jump late in his routine.

Stojko, champion in 1994 and 1995, tumbled trying a quadruple jump. Both scored good marks for technique but Eldredge received slightly better scores than the Canadian for artistry and was first on the cards of five of the seven judges.
Eldredge showed no effects of his injury until the triple axel late in his routine.
"I was feeling a little tired and I pulled it a little too hard," he explained.
"But I wasn't favouring the ankle. Since yesterday it has felt 90 percent fine."
